buyer_question: We are considering requests-html for scraping JavaScript-heavy pages. Does the advertised 'Full JavaScript support' via render() actually work today on a supported Python, and is the project's CI alive?

claims.text: The package requests-html can be installed with the exact command `pipenv install requests-html` (equivalently `pip install requests-html`).
claims.source_quote:
Installation
============

.. code-block:: shell

    $ pipenv install requests-html
    ✨🍰✨
claims.probe_hint: In a fresh venv, `pip install requests-html`; check exit code 0 and that `import requests_html` succeeds.

claims.text: requests-html supports Python 3.6 and above (i.e. it installs and imports on any Python >= 3.6, including current releases).
claims.probe_hint: Install and `import requests_html` on the current Python (3.12/3.13); check for install-time or import-time failures from stale pinned dependencies.

claims.text: The library provides full JavaScript support: calling `r.html.render()` downloads Chromium (via pyppeteer) and renders the page's dynamic JavaScript content.
claims.source_quote: - **Full JavaScript support**! (Using Chromium, thanks to pyppeteer)
claims.probe_hint: Run `HTMLSession().get(...)` on a JS-rendered page then `r.html.render()`. Expect failure today: pyppeteer is unmaintained (#573) and render() is broken for many users (#540, #322, #207); the pinned Chromium download endpoint is dead.

claims.text: The first time `render()` is run it downloads Chromium into the user's home directory (~/.pyppeteer/), and this happens only once.
claims.source_quote:
Note, the first time you ever run the ``render()`` method, it will download
Chromium into your home directory (e.g. ``~/.pyppeteer/``). This only happens
once.
claims.probe_hint: In a clean home dir, call render() and observe whether the Chromium download succeeds; pyppeteer's chromium download URL (storage.googleapis.com chromium-browser-snapshots pin) has been removed.

claims.text: The Travis CI badge asserts the master branch currently builds and passes on travis-ci.com.
claims.probe_hint: GET the badge URL / target page; travis-ci.com OSS builds ended in 2021, so check whether any recent build exists (repo last pushed 2024).

claims.text: A GET request via `HTMLSession` exposes `r.html.links`, which returns the set of all links on the page (anchors excluded).
claims.source_quote:
Grab a list of all links on the page, as–is (anchors excluded):

.. code-block:: pycon

    >>> r.html.links
claims.probe_hint: Serve a small local HTML file with 3 <a href> links via http.server; `HTMLSession().get(url).html.links` should return exactly that set of hrefs (no network flakiness).

claims.text: `r.html.search('Python is a {} language')[0]` on the python.org homepage returns the string 'programming'.
claims.probe_hint: GET https://python.org/ and run the search; alternatively verify the search() API against a local page containing the sentence, asserting the capture equals 'programming'.

claims.text: Async is supported: `AsyncHTMLSession().run(coro1, coro2, coro3)` executes multiple async GET requests and returns a list of Response objects.
claims.source_quote:
>>> results = asession.run(get_pythonorg, get_reddit, get_google)
    >>> results # check the requests all returned a 200 (success) code
    [<Response [200]>, <Response [200]>, <Response [200]>]
claims.probe_hint: Run AsyncHTMLSession against three local endpoints; assert a list of 3 responses with status_code 200.

claims.text: The library works without Requests: `HTML(html="<a href='https://httpbin.org'>").links` returns `{'https://httpbin.org'}`.
claims.source_quote:
>>> from requests_html import HTML
    >>> doc = """<a href='https://httpbin.org'>"""
    >>> html = HTML(html=doc)
    >>> html.links
    {'https://httpbin.org'}
claims.probe_hint: Run exactly this snippet offline; assert the returned set equals {'https://httpbin.org'}.

claims.text: XPath selectors are supported via `r.html.xpath(...)`, returning matching Element objects.
claims.source_quote:
XPath is also supported:

.. code-block:: pycon

   >>> r.html.xpath('/html/body/div[1]/a')
claims.probe_hint: On a local page, `html.xpath('//a')` should return a non-empty list of Element objects with expected href attrs.

claims.text: CSS selectors are supported via `r.html.find(selector, first=True)`, and element `.text`, `.attrs`, and `.absolute_links` work as shown.
claims.source_quote:
Select an element with a CSS Selector:

.. code-block:: pycon

    >>> about = r.html.find('#about', first=True)
claims.probe_hint: On a local page with a known #about element, assert find('#about', first=True).text and .attrs match the authored HTML.
